stage1.impression: A ribbed red glass pendant hangs over an oak table with a pale runner, a white dish and a cluster of small fruit. The pool of light on the runner and dish is the brightest thing in the frame and pulls the eye off the lamp, while the shade, the black fins and the top 55% of the frame sink into a flat brown murk.

blocking_9: The lamp must be the brightest read in the frame. Now the shade body has median 25.5 (region 300,180,600,400) and the runner has median 205 (50,800,450,960), an 8:1 ratio the wrong way.

The light on the table must read as the lamp's coloured light. The pool now measures near neutral white (runner R/G/B 221/203/189, dish 237/224/212), so the brief, 'its coloured light on the table', is not visible.
The black heat-sink fins must hold form. Region 380,120,520,200 is 78.6% crushed (median 0.1).

The wall must have direction and separate from the shade's flanks. Wall 600,50,880,500 has lum range 14.9 and median 28.6, the shade's side 290,300,330,380 is 16.2 against wall ~18.6, so the silhouette almost dissolves.
Dead band between the shade's rim (y~395) and the table edge (y~640) is about 22% of the frame with nothing in it.

changes.problem: The pale runner and white dish turn the pool into a near-white hotspot that outshines the lamp and washes out its colour.

change.to: no runner; pears only, on bare veneer

changes.expected: The pool falls on wood only and drops to roughly 110-150 at its centre. The pears stay as the single scale cue, with no white mass competing with the shade.

changes.problem: The light oak is a second bright, warm surface that matches the lamp's warmth and flattens the contrast between pool and surround.
changes.expected: The foreground table drops to roughly 70-110 median. The pool's edge reads as light on a dark surface.

changes.problem: The shade's terraced edges, the hero, sit at median 25.5 with only a central hotspot, so the stacked glowing lines the design depends on barely register.

evidence.measured: lum_median 25.5, p95 90; horizontal profile 19.6, 16.4, 24.6, 30.6, 30.6, 25.8, 17.7, 17.3; hotspot 400,230,500,290 already 12.4% clipped

changes.expected: The ring edges across the shade read as distinct lit lines. Shade median about 40-60.

changes.problem: The hotspot inside the shade is already clipping, and raising the glow will widen the clipping unless exposure gives back some headroom.
changes.expected: With c3, the inner hotspot keeps detail.

changes.problem: The dusk world is too weak to give the wall any cool counter-tone or gradient, so the upper frame is one muddy brown.
changes.expected: The wall picks up a faint blue-grey dusk tone.

changes.problem: The room fill does not reach the wall behind the shade, so the shade's flanks are darker than the wall and the silhouette dissolves.

evidence.measured: shade flank lum_median 16.2 against adjacent wall about 18.6

changes.expected: The wall behind the lamp rises to median about 28-40.

changes.problem: The anodised fins of the heat sink are a black blob with no edges, so the seven-fin stack is lost.

change.to: small rectangular area light 300 x 300 mm, about 600 mm behind and 300 mm above the lamp, camera-left, aimed at the fin stack, neutral 4000 K, about 15 W, camera-invisible

changes.expected: Each fin's edge catches a thin grey line about 40-90 bright.

changes.problem: The empty band between the shade's rim and the table is about 22% of a portrait frame, so the lamp and its pool read as two separate pictures.

evidence.measured: lum_median about 20 across the band, with no content

changes.expected: Retarget so the shade's top fin sits about 12% from the top and the pears about 12% from the bottom.

out_of_scope.request: Check that the shade's tint renders as amber, not red.
out_of_scope.why: The card describes amber-tinted acrylic, but the shade measures pure red (flank RGB 57/5/0, body 65/15/4). The tint is fixed, so it needs a check against the maker's transmission data.

out_of_scope.request: More of the shade's colour in the pool on the table.
out_of_scope.why: The pool is near white because the COB fires straight down through the louvre and not through the acrylic. Coloured light on the table would need a change to the lamp's optics, which is fixed.

duel.why: B's ribbed red glass glows from within and throws a real pool of warm light onto the table, so the lamp's light is the subject. That reads as a photograph with mood, and the stepped ribbing gives the object its own identity. A's shade is unlit and reads as a glossy CG dome floating over a dim, flatly lit room. It is also a generic pendant and its light does nothing, though B's odd domed plate and loose pears still give away the render.
